# GGUF reference fixture

`reference.gguf` is a 16 KiB synthetic file generated by the upstream GGUFWriter.
It contains all 35 block layouts registered in the pinned upstream version,
all scalar metadata types and their homogeneous arrays. Tensor bytes are a
deterministic pattern, not numerically meaningful model weights.
`reference.json` records upstream GGUFReader results and samples from the start,
middle and end of every tensor. Rust tests consume these files without Python,
network access, CUDA or actual model downloads.

Upstream: [llama.cpp c550d2f60bde72df19fcef1fef627895095b8ba8](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/tree/c550d2f60bde72df19fcef1fef627895095b8ba8/gguf-py).
Generation used Python 3.12 and NumPy 2.5.2. Place that checkout's `gguf-py`
directory on `PYTHONPATH`, then run from the RustInfer root:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/path/to/llama.cpp/gguf-py python crates/infer-gguf/tests/fixtures/gguf/generate.py
cargo test -p infer-gguf --lib reader
cargo test -p infer-worker --no-default-features --test gguf
cargo test -p infer-gguf --doc
```

To compare a real file, generate its independent manifest and explicitly enable
the ignored integration test. Use an **absolute** manifest path, because Cargo
runs integration tests from the crate directory:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/path/to/llama.cpp/gguf-py python crates/infer-gguf/tests/fixtures/gguf/generate.py \
  --model /absolute/path/model.gguf --output /tmp/model.reference.json
RUSTINFER_GGUF_REFERENCE=/tmp/model.reference.json \
  cargo test -p infer-worker --no-default-features --test gguf gguf_local_model -- --ignored --nocapture
```

The comparison covers every metadata value and type, tensor name, dimension,
encoding, offset and byte length, plus three small byte slices per tensor.
It does not dequantize weights, evaluate the model, or hash the whole file.
Hand-encoded unit fixtures separately test nested/empty arrays, v2, non-power-of-two
alignment, reordered tensor ranges, malformed data and resource budgets.
